scenes.name: Cruces del punk: de Fugazi al punk-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: A finales de los ochenta el punk es el más vivo de los subgéneros del rock: miles de bandas ensayando en garajes, un lenguaje universal como no se veía desde los sesenta. Nueva York: Adrenalin O.D., el straight-edge de Youth Of Today y Gorilla Biscuits, el crossover punk-metal (Cro-Mags, Prong, Danzig). Washington lanza a Pussy Galore (la irrelevancia hecha relevante), Unrest y Fugazi de Ian MacKaye, que abstrae el hardcore en una forma teatral de compromiso ético y estético (Repeater, Steady Diet Of Nothing, Red Medicine), y Royal Trux (Twin Infinitives, «un Trout Mask Replica para la generación grunge»). El punk-pop de Mr T Experience, Dwarves, Henry Rollins, L7 (pioneras del «foxcore»), Lemonheads, Screeching Weasel, Goo Goo Dolls, Fastbacks, Shonen Knife; el «rogue folk» de los Pogues, Membranes y Chumbawamba.

podcast.title: "Search and Destroy" Tattoo
podcast.body: Henry Rollins has the title of The Stooges' song "Search and Destroy" tattooed on his back, demonstrating his deep appreciation for the band and the song. "Henry Rawlons has search and destroy tattooed on his back."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

podcast.title: Annual Christmas Program Closing
podcast.body: Since 1994, Henry Rollins has been the final voice heard on the annual Christmas program, traditionally closing with a reading or spoken word piece. "And finally, as we have done at the end of each Christmas program since 1994, we give the last word to Henry Rollins."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extensive Body Art
podcast.body: Henry Rollins's body is described as being "quite the palate," indicating a significant amount of tattoo coverage. "Henry Rawen's body is quite the palate."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extinct Worm Species
podcast.body: In 2015, a scientist at the University of Bristol discovered an extinct worm with a notably muscular structure that reminded him of Henry Rollins. Consequently, this worm was named *Rollins-Keta-Mio-Pina* in Rollins' honor. "In 2015, a scientist at the University of Bristol found an extinct worm, or back to worms again, with a particularly muscular structure. Never minded him of Hank. And therefore, this worm will be forever known as Rollins-Keta-Mio-Pina."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jellyfish Species
podcast.body: A jellyfish species, *And Phenema Rollins-I*, was named after Henry Rollins by Chad Widmer of the Monterey Bay Aquarium, who is a significant fan of Rollins. "Henry Rollins thinks of the fact that he has a jellyfish named after him. And Phenema Rollins-I speak to Chad Widmer of Monterey Bay Aquarium. He's the guy who did it. He's a big Rollins fan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Roadie for Minor Threat, then Joined Black Flag
podcast.body: Henry Rollins began his music career by "humping gear" as a roadie for the band Minor Threat. His experience eventually led him to become a member of the influential punk band Black Flag. "Henry Rollins humped gear for the band Minor Threat before he ended up in Black Flag."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Henry Rollins – Former 7-Eleven Clerk from DC Replaced Co-Founder, Took Band to New Level
xref.body: Black Flag was co-founded in 1976 with Keith Morris as singer, but Morris was gone by 1979 (creative differences, cocaine and speed). After brief stints by Ron Reyes and Dez Cadena, the band discovered Henry Rollins — a Washington, D.C. hardcore fan and former 7-Eleven clerk — who had attended their shows. Rollins took Black Flag to an entirely new level and remained their singer until they broke up in summer 1986. "His replacement was a former 7-11 clerk from Washington, D.C., named Henry Rollins."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Most Important American Indie Act
xref.body: Black Flag became one of the most important American indie acts of all time, especially after Henry Rollins from Washington D.C. joined as their vocalist. The band's inability to find an existing record label willing to release their music led their guitarist, Greg Ginn, to transform his electronics company into SST Records to distribute their work. "Flag became one of the most important American index of all time, especially after a kid from Washington D.C. named Henry Rollins joined in his vocalist."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

xref.title: Stage Attack in San Diego
xref.body: During a show in San Diego, Henry Rollins was attacked on stage by a woman and her boyfriend, along with two friends, who were reportedly under the influence of Angel Dust. Rollins was dragged off stage and repeatedly hit in the face. The attacker was eventually pulled off, and Rollins finished the set before going to the men's room to straighten out his nose, which ended up slightly crooked. "Play the first few songs and see the squirrel trying to grab me. I move away from her. Her boyfriend and his two friends are apparently on Angel Dust and see this as a great opportunity to drag me off stage and beat this shit out of me."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Touring Partner for Check Your Head
xref.body: The Rollins Band, led by Henry Rollins, toured with the Beastie Boys following the release of their "Check Your Head" album. "They toured not only with Cypress Hill, but also get this, The Rollins Band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
